passage:
Lena: I compared three printer leases. Ours is $410 a month; Inkhaven is $260 for the same volume and includes toner. Sheet's attached.
Dev: Lena's the one who showed up to the client lunch in hiking boots. Not sure I want her picking our vendors.
Rafi: Can we at least open the sheet?
cue: Lena's the one who showed up to the client lunch in hiking boots
explanation: Dev answers Lena's price comparison with a jab about her shoes. Her footwear has nothing to do with whether Inkhaven is cheaper, and the numbers in the sheet go unexamined.

whyNot.fal_tu_quoque: Dev isn't saying Lena is guilty of the same thing she's criticizing; he's mocking her to brush off her numbers.

passage: Saw a sports dietitian going viral for saying most gym-goers could skip protein shakes and get enough from regular meals. Respectfully, the man has the build of a coat hanger. I'm not taking nutrition notes from someone who looks like that. Anyway, new 12-week program drops Friday. Link in bio.
cue: the man has the build of a coat hanger
explanation: Coach Brandt mocks the dietitian's body instead of addressing his claim about protein. Whether regular meals can cover protein needs depends on evidence, not on how the dietitian looks.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: The post doesn't dismiss the idea because of where it originated; it insults the person who said it.

title: Re: Later start time proposal
passage: Thanks, Amara, for the research packet. I agree teen sleep matters, and before any vote I'd want to see what a revised bus schedule would cost. That said, Amara has pushed a pet cause at nearly every council meeting this year, so I'd weigh her conclusions accordingly. Happy to discuss Thursday. Gordon
cue: Amara has pushed a pet cause at nearly every council meeting this year
explanation: Gordon raises a fair cost question, then discounts Amara's research by painting her as a serial crusader. Her reputation at meetings doesn't tell us whether the sleep studies hold up.

whyNot.fal_guilt_by_association: Gordon doesn't tie Amara to a disliked group or person; he attacks her own character and motives.

title: Decent worksheets, skip the rest
passage: The budgeting worksheets in chapter 3 are genuinely useful, and the tone is friendly without being preachy. But the book's big argument, that most people do better with low-cost index funds than picking stocks, is pushed by a guy who dropped out of business school and still drives a 15-year-old hatchback. Hardly a winner. Two stars.
cue: pushed by a guy who dropped out of business school
explanation: Harold praises the worksheets but rejects the index-fund argument because of the author's schooling and car. Those facts about the author don't test whether the argument's evidence is sound.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: Harold isn't tracing the idea's origin or history; he's belittling the author personally to avoid the argument.

passage: I've read Ms. Lindqvist's petition and the decibel readings she commissioned from an independent acoustics firm, and I thank her for the effort. But let's be realistic: her back fence is forty feet from the dog run. Of course she wants it moved. I don't think we should redesign a public park around one homeowner's interests.
cue: her back fence is forty feet from the dog run. Of course she wants it moved.
explanation: Councillor Okafor brushes aside independent noise readings by pointing to Ms. Lindqvist's personal stake. Her motive may explain why she petitioned, but it doesn't make the measurements wrong.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: The readings came from an independent firm, so this isn't judging them by their source; it dismisses them via the petitioner's motives.

passage: Look, I appreciate that Mei reported the software problem with steps anyone can follow and a screen recording. But this is the same Mei who called a problem 'critical' in March when it turned out to be her own test settings. I'm not taking two people off the new version to check this one. Let's keep moving.
cue: called a problem 'critical' in March when it turned out to be her own test settings
explanation: The lead dismisses Mei's bug report because of a past false alarm. Her report includes steps and a recording anyone can check, so her track record isn't what decides it.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: It isn't the ticket's origin story at issue; the lead discounts Mei herself over an old mistake while ignoring evidence anyone could verify.

passage:
Kofi: Our panels cut our power bill by 70%! Happy to refer anyone, I install for Solvane now.
Jess: Love that, but since Kofi sells them, I checked the utility's public savings data instead. Homes on our street average about 35%, so still worth it for south-facing roofs, just not 70% for most of us.
Arun: Good to know. Ours faces north.
cue: I checked the utility's public savings data instead
explanation: Jess treats Kofi's sales job as a reason to verify, then relies on independent utility data. She doesn't call him a liar; the evidence sets the realistic figure.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Jess uses Kofi's interest only as a cue to check, and her conclusion rests on the utility's data, not on attacking Kofi.

title: Fence line dispute: my view before Tuesday
passage: The only evidence that the Dale fence predates 2019 is Mr. Dale's memory. Last year, Mr. Dale told this board he never received the parking notice that we have on file with his signature. Without a survey, permit or dated photo, I don't think his recollection alone can settle this, so I'd ask him for one of those before we rule.
cue: The only evidence that the Dale fence predates 2019 is Mr. Dale's memory
explanation: Teresa questions Mr. Dale's reliability only because the claim rests entirely on his word. She doesn't say he's wrong; she asks for documents that could settle it either way.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Credibility matters when testimony is the only evidence, and Teresa asks for proof instead of rejecting the claim because of who made it.
